clues: A vertical section oriented at right angles to the median plane.
It separates front structures from back structures of the body.
Also called the frontal plane, it divides anterior from posterior.
A vertical reference plane running lengthwise through the body.
It splits the body symmetrically into right and left sides.
It passes directly through the midline into equal halves.
A relative term used mainly along limbs or tubular structures.
It describes being nearer to a point of origin or attachment.
It means closer to the trunk than the distal end.
A relational term comparing two sides of the body.
It applies when a finding and its reference are on opposite sides.
A left brain lesion affecting the right limb shows this relationship.
A movement typically occurring in the coronal plane.
It moves a limb or digit away from a reference midline.
Raising the arm out to the side away from the body is an example.
A rotational movement involving the bones of the forearm.
It turns the palm of the hand forward or upward.
It positions the palm to face anteriorly from the anatomical stance.
A movement that occurs at the ankle joint.
It lifts the top surface of the foot upward toward the shin.
Raising the toes and front of the foot toward the leg describes it.
A movement involving the foot rather than the hand.
It angles the sole of the foot inward toward the midline.
Turning the plantar surface medially describes this motion.
A specialized motion unique to the first digit of the hand.
It brings the thumb across the palm toward other fingertips.
Touching the thumb pad to the little finger pad demonstrates it.
A compound motion involving multiple basic joint movements.
It moves a limb in a circular path around a joint.
It combines flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction in sequence.
A convention used so everyone describes the body the same way
The body is upright, facing forward, with arms at the sides
Palms face forward and feet are together, the standard reference stance
An imaginary cut used to describe or image the body
It runs vertically from front to back
When it passes through the exact midline it gives equal right and left halves
A word used to describe depth
It describes a structure close to the body surface
Skin is this; the opposite of deep
A term describing the relationship between sides of the body
It refers to structures on the same side
The right arm and right leg are this to each other; the opposite is contralateral
A movement that happens at joints
It usually occurs in the sagittal plane
Bending the elbow so the forearm moves toward the arm; the opposite of extension
